title: Job 35
paragraphs: ¹ Elihu continued speaking: ² "Do you think it is right when you say, 'My righteousness is greater than God's'? ³ For you ask, 'What does it profit you?' and, 'What do I gain by not sinning?' ⁴ I will answer you, and your friends with you.

⁶ If you sin, what do you do against him? If your transgressions multiply, what does it mean to him? ⁷ If you are righteous, what do you give him? What does he receive from your hand? ⁸ Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself; your righteousness benefits only other human beings. ⁹ People cry out under the weight of oppression; they call for relief from the arm of the powerful. ¹⁰ But no one asks, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

¹¹ who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?' ¹² There they cry out, but he gives no answer — because of the pride of evil men. ¹³ Surely God does not listen to empty cries; the Almighty pays no attention to them. ¹⁴ How much less when you say you cannot see him — yet your case lies before him, and you must wait for him. ¹⁵ And now, because his anger has not punished you, and he seems unaware of your great transgression,
¹⁶ Job opens his mouth with empty words; he piles up words without knowledge.
